title: Assessing Children: Age, Anatomy and the PAT
next: Chapter 44, Lesson 2: Breathing emergencies in children and the PCP's airway drugs

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already do infant and child CPR, clear choking airways and bag small patients. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Adapt your approach to the child's age and anatomy
  2. Use the PAT and age-based vital signs to judge sick or not sick
  3. Know what the PCP adds: weight-based thinking and a child-sized Functional Enquiry

Textbook: Chapter 44, PDF pages 3712–3744
slides.say: Welcome to the pediatrics chapter. As EMRs, you've already learned infant and child CPR, how to clear a choking airway, and how to bag a small patient. Now that you're practising as a PCP, children bring new demands. Almost every drug and fluid you give them depends on their weight, so a small mistake can become a big overdose. You also do a deeper assessment, including the Functional Enquiry, which only PCPs do. Today we'll cover three things: how age and anatomy change your approach, how to use the Pediatric Assessment Triangle and normal vital signs, and what the PCP adds to the assessment of a child.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎进入儿科这一章。作为 EMR，你们已经学过婴儿和儿童 CPR、怎么解除异物梗阻、怎么给小病人做球囊面罩通气。现在以 PCP 身份执业，儿童带来新的要求：你给的几乎每一种药和液体都按体重计算，一个小错就可能变成严重过量。你还要做更深入的评估，包括只有 PCP 才做的系统问诊（Functional Enquiry）。今天讲三件事：年龄和解剖如何改变你的接诊方式；怎么用儿科评估三角和正常生命体征；以及 PCP 在儿童评估中多做什么。

slides.title: Meet the child at their age
slides.body:
StageAgeApproach
Neonatefirst monthwarm hands; keep warm
Infantto 12 monthsparent's lap; listen first while quiet
Toddler1–2 yearsfears strangers; limited choices; sore spot last
Preschool3–5 yearsvery literal: plain, gentle words
School age6–12 yearslet them tell the story
Adolescent13–18 yearsprivacy; talk to them; be honest

A calm, involved caregiver means a calmer child. Never blame them.
slides.say: Children change fast, so meet each one at their age. A neonate is in the first month of life; an infant is up to twelve months. Examine an older infant on a parent's lap, with warm hands. Toddlers, one to two years old, are often afraid of strangers. Offer limited choices, because a yes-or-no question usually gets a no, and save the painful part for last. Preschoolers, three to five, take words literally, so use plain, gentle language. School-age children can tell you their own story. Adolescents want privacy and honesty. And remember the caregiver: a calm, involved parent helps keep the child calm.
slides.sayZh: 孩子变化很快，所以要按年龄接诊。新生儿是出生后第一个月；婴儿指十二个月以内。较大的婴儿放在家长腿上检查，手要先捂热。一到两岁的幼儿常常怕生人。给有限的选择，因为是非题多半换来一个「不」，痛的部位留到最后查。三到五岁的学龄前儿童按字面理解话语，所以要用直白、温和的话。学龄儿童能自己讲经过。青少年需要隐私和坦诚。也别忘了照护者：一个冷静、参与进来的家长能帮孩子保持平静。

slides.title: Smaller airway, faster crash
slides.body:
Airwaynarrow, big tonguenarrowest at the cricoid
Breathingsoft ribs, belly breathingretractions show early
Heartsmall stroke volumespeeds up to compensate
  • Infants breathe through the nose for the first 4–6 months
  • Head is 2/3 of adult size: heat loss, lands head-first
slides.say: Why do children crash differently? Start with the airway. It's narrow, and the tongue is big for the mouth, so a little swelling, some mucus or a small object blocks it easily. The narrowest point is lower than in adults, at the cricoid ring below the vocal cords. For the first four to six months, infants breathe mainly through the nose, so a blocked nose alone can cause real distress. The ribs are soft, so you see retractions early, and infants normally breathe with the belly. The heart can't pump much more blood per beat, so the child raises the heart rate to compensate. And the large head loses heat quickly.
slides.sayZh: 孩子为什么会以不同的方式垮掉？先看气道：气道细，舌头相对口腔很大，一点肿胀、一点黏液或一个小物件就容易堵住。最窄处比成人低，在声带下方的环状软骨处。出生后头四到六个月，婴儿主要经鼻呼吸，所以光是鼻子堵了就可能造成明显窘迫。肋骨软，吸凹出现得早；婴儿平时就是腹式呼吸。心脏每搏能多泵出的血很有限，所以孩子靠加快心率来代偿。另外，大大的头部散热很快。

slides.title: Injuries follow the anatomy
slides.body:
• Serious trauma, most to least: head, abdomen, chest
  • Liver and spleen sit below the ribs: big bleeds
  • Bendy chest: lungs and heart hurt without rib fractures
  • Bones weaker than ligaments: fractures, not sprains
  • Cord injury possible with a normal-looking spine

Significant mechanism? Assume a spinal injury and restrict motion.
slides.say: The same anatomy shapes injuries. In serious pediatric trauma, the head is injured most often, then the abdomen, then the chest. The liver and spleen sit below the ribs with little protection, and they bleed a lot. The chest wall bends instead of breaking, so the lungs and heart can be badly hurt without a single rib fracture. Bones are weaker than ligaments, so children get fractures, including growth plate fractures, more often than sprains. Spinal ligaments are loose, so the cord can be injured even when the bones look normal. So with a significant mechanism, assume a spinal injury and restrict motion.
slides.sayZh: 同样的解剖也决定了损伤的样子。儿童严重创伤中，最常受伤的是头，其次是腹部，再次是胸部。肝和脾在肋缘以下、缺少保护，出血量大。胸壁会弯而不会断，所以肺和心脏可能严重受伤，却一根肋骨都没断。骨头比韧带弱，所以孩子骨折（包括生长板骨折）比扭伤多见。脊柱韧带松弛，即使骨头看起来正常，脊髓也可能受伤。所以只要受伤机制明显，就当作有脊柱损伤，做脊柱运动限制。

slides.title: The PAT: sick or not sick?
slides.body:
AppearanceTICLS: tone, interactiveness, consolability, look, speech/cryusually most important
Work of breathingsounds, position, retractions, flaringtells more than the rate
Circulation to skinpale, mottled, bluemirrors core perfusion

Hands off, from the doorway, before you touch the child.
slides.say: The Pediatric Assessment Triangle, or PAT, is a hands-off look from the doorway that answers one question: is this child sick or not sick? It has three sides. Appearance is usually the most important. Use TICLS: tone, interactiveness, consolability, look or gaze, and speech or cry. A limp child who won't look at you is sick. Work of breathing tells you more than the breathing rate: listen for abnormal sounds and look at position, retractions and nasal flaring. Circulation to the skin shows how well the core is perfused. Do this before you touch the child, because your touch may upset them and change what you see.
slides.sayZh: 儿科评估三角（PAT）是在门口不接触患儿的一眼观察，只回答一个问题：这个孩子病重还是不重？它有三条边。外观通常最重要，用 TICLS：肌张力、互动、可安抚性、眼神注视、言语或哭声。一个软塌塌、不看你的孩子就是病重。呼吸做功比呼吸频率更有信息量：听有没有异常声音，看体位、吸凹和鼻翼扇动。皮肤循环反映核心灌注好不好。这些要在碰孩子之前做完，因为你一碰，孩子可能就闹起来，你看到的东西也就变了。

slides.title: What breathing and skin tell you
slides.body:
You see or hearIt points to
Snoringmouth and throat
Stridor, muffled voiceupper airway, near the cords
Wheezesmall lower airways
Gruntingmoderate to severe hypoxia
Sniffing / tripod positionsevere obstruction / accessory muscles
Pale → mottled → blueearly → worse → late failure

Blue hands and feet in a cold baby under 2 months can be normal (acrocyanosis).
slides.say: Let's decode what you see and hear. Snoring comes from the mouth and throat. Stridor, or a muffled, hoarse voice, comes from the upper airway around the vocal cords. Wheezing comes from the small lower airways. Grunting is a short, low sound at the end of each breath out, and it suggests moderate to severe hypoxia. A child in the sniffing position has a severe upper airway blockage; a tripod position means they're using accessory muscles. For the skin, pallor is often the first sign of shock, mottling is worse, and true cyanosis is late. Blue hands and feet in a cold baby under two months can be normal.
slides.sayZh: 来解读你看到和听到的东西。鼾声来自口咽部。喘鸣，或声音发闷、嘶哑，来自声带附近的上气道。哮鸣来自下面的小气道。呻吟是每次呼气末一声短而低的声音，提示中到重度缺氧。孩子取嗅物位说明上气道严重梗阻；三脚架位说明在动用辅助呼吸肌。皮肤方面，苍白常是休克最早的征象，花斑更重，真正的发绀是晚期表现。两个月以下的婴儿受冷时手脚发青可以是正常的。

slides.q: From the doorway, which finding in a 9-month-old worries you most?
options: Crying loudly and clinging to the parent as you approach
A glassy stare that doesn't follow faces, with grunting
Pink skin and a runny nose
slides.say: Let's check. From the doorway, which finding in a nine-month-old worries you most? A, crying loudly and clinging to the parent as you approach. B, a glassy stare that doesn't follow faces, with grunting. C, fast breathing while crying. D, pink skin and a runny nose. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来检验一下。站在门口，一个九个月大的婴儿，哪个表现最让你担心？A，你走近时大声哭、紧抱家长；B，眼神呆滞、不追随人脸，伴有呻吟；C，哭的时候呼吸快；D，皮肤红润、流鼻涕。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A glassy stare that doesn't follow faces is an abnormal appearance, the most important side of the PAT, and grunting suggests moderate to severe hypoxia. This child is sick. A is a normal, healthy reaction to a stranger: good tone, good interaction, a strong cry. C is expected, because crying speeds up breathing. D shows normal skin circulation and, at nine months, a runny nose alone doesn't threaten the airway.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。眼神呆滞、不追随人脸属于外观异常，而外观是 PAT 最重要的一边；呻吟提示中到重度缺氧。这个孩子病重。A 是见到陌生人时正常、健康的反应：肌张力好、有互动、哭声有力。C 在意料之中，哭本来就会让呼吸变快。D 皮肤循环正常，九个月大时单纯流鼻涕并不威胁气道。

slides.title: Weight first: every dose depends on it
slides.body:
1. Ask the caregiver the weight, and how recent it is
  2. Or use a length-based tape: red end at the head
  3. Read the weight and equipment sizes at the heel
  4. Longer than the tape? Use adult equipment and doses

Children are at high risk of dosing errors: use a reference card or app, not your memory.
slides.say: Early in the call, estimate the child's weight, because almost everything you give as a PCP depends on it: drug doses, fluid volumes and equipment sizes. Ask the caregiver what the child weighs and how recent that number is. Or use a length-based tape: put the red end at the head, and read the weight and equipment sizes at the heel. If the child is longer than the tape, use adult equipment and doses. The book warns that children are at high risk of medication errors, because weights are hard to estimate and every dose needs a calculation. So use a reference card or app, not your memory.
slides.sayZh: 接诊早期就要估算孩子的体重，因为你作为 PCP 给的几乎一切都取决于它：药物剂量、液体量和器械尺寸。问照护者孩子多重、这个数字是多久以前的。或者用身长复苏尺：红色一端对齐头顶，在足跟处读出体重和器械尺寸。孩子比尺子还长，就用成人器械和成人剂量。书里提醒，儿童用药出错的风险很高，因为体重难估、每个剂量都要计算。所以用参考卡或手机应用，别靠记忆。

slides.title: Normal vital signs by age
slides.body:
AgeRRHR awakeSystolic
Neonate (0–1 mo)30–60100–20567–84
Infant (1–12 mo)30–53100–18072–104
Toddler (1–2 y)22–3798–14086–106
Preschool (3–5 y)20–2880–12089–112
School age (6–12 y)18–2575–11897–120
Adolescent12–2060–100110–131

Lowest acceptable systolic, ages 1–10: 70 + (2 × age in years)
slides.say: Here are the textbook's normal ranges. Notice the pattern: the younger the child, the faster the breathing and heart rate, and the lower the blood pressure. A newborn breathes thirty to sixty times a minute; a teenager twelve to twenty. For children aged one to ten, there's a formula for the lowest acceptable systolic pressure: seventy plus two times the age in years. A four-year-old should have at least seventy-eight. Below that, the child is in decompensated shock. But a normal pressure doesn't rule out shock, because children hold their pressure until very late.
slides.sayZh: 这是教科书给的正常范围。注意规律：孩子越小，呼吸和心率越快，血压越低。新生儿每分钟呼吸三十到六十次，青少年十二到二十次。一到十岁的孩子，有个最低可接受收缩压的公式：七十加上两倍的年龄（岁）。四岁孩子至少应有七十八。低于这个数，就是失代偿性休克。但血压正常并不能排除休克，因为孩子会把血压撑到很晚。

slides.title: Hands on: the primary assessment
slides.body:
• Breathing: count 30 seconds, then double it
  • Infants may pause under 20 s: short counts read low
  • No radial or brachial pulse? Femoral (small child) or carotid (older)
  • Capillary refill: normal under 3 seconds
  • BP cuff 2/3 of the upper arm; one try, then move on
  • AVPU, then pupils, then movement

Suction: don't linger in the throat; the vagal reflex can drop the heart rate.
slides.say: Now hands on. Count breathing for thirty seconds and double it. Healthy infants can pause for less than twenty seconds, so a short count may read falsely low. If you can't find a radial or brachial pulse, feel a central one: the femoral in infants and small children, the carotid in older ones. Capillary refill should be under three seconds, but a cold room slows it too. Use a cuff two-thirds the length of the upper arm, and make one attempt at the blood pressure, then move on. Check AVPU, then the pupils, then movement. And when you suction, don't leave the tip in the throat: the vagal reflex can slow the heart.
slides.sayZh: 现在上手检查。呼吸数三十秒再乘二。健康婴儿可以有短于二十秒的呼吸暂停，数得太短会偏低。摸不到桡动脉或肱动脉，就摸中心脉搏：婴儿和小孩子摸股动脉，大一些的孩子摸颈动脉。毛细血管再充盈正常应在三秒以内，但冷的环境也会让它变慢。袖带宽度取上臂长度的三分之二；血压只试测一次，然后继续往下评估。先查 AVPU，再看瞳孔，再看肢体活动。吸引时别把吸引头一直留在咽部：迷走反射会让心率掉下来。

slides.q: A drowsy 4-year-old has HR 170, capillary refill of 4 seconds and a systolic BP of 74. How do you interpret this?
options: Normal BP for age, so compensated shock at most
Normal findings for a child who has been crying
Shock can't be judged in a child without a second BP
slides.say: Here's a clinical question. A drowsy four-year-old has a heart rate of one hundred seventy, a capillary refill of four seconds and a systolic pressure of seventy-four. How do you interpret this? A, the blood pressure is normal for age, so compensated shock at most. B, decompensated shock, because the systolic is below seventy plus two times four, which is seventy-eight. C, normal findings for a child who has been crying. D, shock can't be judged in a child without a second blood pressure. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道临床题。一个四岁孩子昏昏欲睡，心率一百七十，毛细血管再充盈四秒，收缩压七十四。你怎么解读？A，血压对这个年龄正常，最多是代偿性休克；B，失代偿性休克，因为收缩压低于七十加二乘四，也就是七十八；C，哭过的孩子出现这些都正常；D，没有第二次血压就无法判断儿童休克。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. For ages one to ten, the lowest acceptable systolic is seventy plus two times the age; for a four-year-old that's seventy-eight, so seventy-four is hypotension, which means decompensated shock. The drowsiness, fast heart rate and slow refill all fit. A uses the wrong cut-off. C is wrong because this child is drowsy, not crying. D is wrong: the book says make one attempt at a blood pressure and then judge the whole picture, and this picture is clear.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。一到十岁最低可接受收缩压是七十加两倍年龄，四岁就是七十八，所以七十四属于低血压，也就是失代偿性休克。嗜睡、心率快、再充盈慢都与之相符。A 用错了界值。C 错在这个孩子是嗜睡，不是在哭。D 也不对：书里说血压只试测一次，然后看整体表现，而这里的整体表现已经很清楚。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: assessing a child
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • PAT and primary survey; fix problems as found
  • Vital signs, SpO₂ and blood glucose
  • History; for pain, BC grading: OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • Head-to-toe exam; reassess; transport

PCP adds

  • Functional Enquiry: 9 systems (PCP only)
  • Weight → PCP drug doses and fluid volumes
  • Vascular access when a protocol calls for it
  • Reassess after every drug and bolus
slides.say: So how does your assessment of a child change when you step up? The left column is what every licence level does: the PAT and primary survey, vital signs with oxygen saturation and blood glucose, a history, using OPQRRRST or LOTARP for pain, a head-to-toe exam, then reassessment and transport. The right column is new for you. In BC's grading, the Functional Enquiry is PCP only. You turn the child's weight into PCP drug doses and fluid volumes. You start vascular access when a protocol calls for it. And because you're now giving drugs and fluids, you reassess after every one.
slides.sayZh: 升到 PCP 之后，你对儿童的评估有什么变化？左栏是所有执照级别都做的：PAT 和初级评估；生命体征，包括血氧和血糖；采集病史，问疼痛时用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP；从头到脚体检，然后复评、转运。右栏是你的新内容：在 BC 评分标准里，系统问诊（Functional Enquiry）只有 PCP 做；你要把孩子的体重换算成 PCP 药物剂量和液体量；规程需要时建立血管通路；而且既然你现在会给药、给液体，每给一次都要复评。

slides.title: The Functional Enquiry, child-sized
slides.body:
SystemAsk the child or caregiver, e.g.
General healthrecent illness, fever, eating, energy
CNSsleepier, irritable, seizure, headache
Respiratorycough, noisy breathing, sick contacts
Cardiovascularcolour changes, sweating with feeds
GI / GUvomiting, diarrhea, wet diapers, pain
Skin, MSKrash, bruises, limping, not using a limb
Endocrine, EENTthirst, diabetes; ear pulling, sore throat

BC grading: a missed system costs up to 5%, 15% maximum. No deduction if no history is available.
slides.say: BC's grading lists nine systems for the PCP's Functional Enquiry: general health, the central nervous system, respiratory, cardiovascular, GI and GU, skin, musculoskeletal, endocrine, and eyes, ears, nose and throat. With a child, you ask about the same systems in child-sized words, often through the caregiver. Has she been eating and drinking? How many wet diapers today? Is he sleepier or crankier than usual? Any coughing, noisy breathing, or sweating with feeds? A rash, a limp, or pulling at an ear? Skipping a system costs up to five percent, with a maximum of fifteen percent for the whole enquiry. If no history is available, there's no deduction.
slides.sayZh: BC 评分标准给 PCP 的系统问诊列了九个系统：全身健康、中枢神经、呼吸、心血管、消化和泌尿生殖、皮肤、肌肉骨骼、内分泌，以及眼耳鼻喉。面对孩子，问的还是这些系统，只是换成孩子听得懂的话，而且常常要通过照护者来问。她最近吃喝怎么样？今天换了几片湿尿布？他比平时更嗜睡、更闹吗？有没有咳嗽、呼吸有声音、吃奶时出汗？有没有皮疹、走路瘸、老拽耳朵？漏掉一个系统最多扣百分之五，整个系统问诊最多扣百分之十五。如果无法获得病史，就不扣分。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A wrong weight means a wrong dose: confirm it first
  • Milligrams are not millilitres: say both out loud
  • Normal SpO₂ or BP does not rule out distress or shock
  • A tired child's rate can fall back to "normal"
  • Pain is a vital sign: assess, treat, reassess
  • Vitals every 5 min if unstable, every 15 min if stable
slides.say: Now the new risks at PCP level. A wrong weight means a wrong dose, so confirm the weight before any drug. Milligrams aren't millilitres: say the dose and the volume out loud with your partner. A normal saturation or blood pressure doesn't mean the child is fine; they may be working very hard to keep it there. A breathing rate that falls back to normal in a child who was working hard may mean exhaustion, not improvement. Pain is a vital sign: assess it, treat it, and reassess it. And repeat vital signs every five minutes if the child is unstable, every fifteen if stable.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 层面的新风险。体重错了，剂量就错了，所以给任何药之前先确认体重。毫克不是毫升：和搭档把剂量和体积都大声说出来。血氧或血压正常不代表孩子没事，他可能正拼命代偿才维持住。一个原本呼吸很费力的孩子，呼吸频率「回到正常」可能是累垮了，而不是好转。疼痛是生命体征：评估它、处理它、再复评。孩子不稳定时每五分钟复测生命体征，稳定时每十五分钟一次。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Pain history: book uses OPQRST; BC grading uses OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • Lungs: book listens midaxillary; BC wants 6 points front or back
  • Low sugar: BC treats BGL < 4.0 at every age
  • Suction: BC limits 10 s in a child, 5 s in an infant
  • Book's opioids and benzodiazepines for pain: not BC EMR/PCP
slides.say: A few points where the exam follows BC, not the book. For pain, the book teaches OPQRST; BC's grading expects either OPQRRRST or LOTARP. The book listens to a child's chest at the midaxillary line; BC expects at least six points on the front or six on the back. The book uses different low-sugar cut-offs for newborns and older children; BC treats a blood glucose under four point zero the same way at every age. BC limits suctioning to ten seconds in a child and five seconds in an infant. And the book mentions opioids and benzodiazepines for children's pain; those aren't in BC's EMR or PCP scope.
slides.sayZh: 有几处考试按 BC，不按书。问疼痛时书里教 OPQRST，BC 评分要求用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP 其中一个。书里给孩子听诊放在腋中线，BC 要求前胸至少六个点或后背六个点。书里对新生儿和大一些的孩子用不同的低血糖界值，BC 各年龄一律按血糖低于四点零处理。BC 规定吸引时间儿童不超过十秒、婴儿不超过五秒。另外书里提到用阿片类和苯二氮卓类给孩子止痛，这些不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. PAT from the doorway: appearance, work of breathing, skin
  2. Lowest systolic (1–10 y) = 70 + 2 × age; a normal BP doesn't rule out shock
  3. PCP adds weight-based doses and the Functional Enquiry; reassess often

Next: breathing emergencies in children and the PCP's airway drugs
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: start every child with the PAT from the doorway: appearance, work of breathing and circulation to the skin, and decide sick or not sick before you touch. Two: for ages one to ten, the lowest acceptable systolic is seventy plus two times the age, but a normal pressure never rules out shock. Three: as a PCP, you turn weight into doses, you add the Functional Enquiry in child-sized words, and you reassess after everything you give. Next lesson: breathing emergencies in children, and the PCP drugs you'll use. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，每个孩子都从门口的 PAT 开始：外观、呼吸做功、皮肤循环，在碰孩子之前先判断病重还是不重。二，一到十岁最低可接受收缩压是七十加两倍年龄，但血压正常永远不能排除休克。三，作为 PCP，你要把体重换算成剂量，用孩子听得懂的话做系统问诊，每给一样东西都要复评。下节课讲儿童呼吸急症，以及你会用到的 PCP 药物。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
